category: Capture Tcl user-action commands (journaled GUI commands) and session/application Tcl commands
description: The Capture Tcl commands that mirror interactive actions on the schematic page and in the Project Manager, as listed in 'Appendix A: Capture Commands List' of the Cadence application note 'OrCAD Capture Tcl/Tk Extensions'. With journaling on (SetOptionBool Journaling TRUE) Capture echoes these commands for every manual action, e.g. 'PlaceWire 4.00 1.00 6.00 1.00'. They take space-separated Tcl arguments (the appendix shows C-style signatures), coordinates in page units as echoed by the journal, and are case-sensitive. Database-level Dbo* commands are catalogued separately.

tools.name: PlacePart
tools.description: Places a part from a library at a page location, exactly as Place > Part does. The journal records the library path, package name and device designator, so recording one placement is the easiest way to get the exact arguments for a script.

parameters.name: libName
parameters.description: Full path of the .olb (brace-quote Windows paths).

parameters.name: pkgName / device
parameters.description: Package (part) name and device designator (section) as journaled.

tools.example:
SetOptionBool Journaling TRUE
# place one resistor by hand, copy the echoed line, then:
PlacePart 2.00 1.00 {C:/Cadence/SPB_17.4/tools/capture/library/discrete.olb} R {} FALSE
tools.notes: Related: PlacePartWithDialog x y opens the Place Part dialog at a location; PlacePartEx libName pkgName deviceDesignator isConvert and PlaceNew libName name ?deviceIndex? attach a part to the cursor. Finish multi-placement modes with EndPlace.

tools.name: ReplacePart
tools.description: Replaces the selected part instance(s) with another part from a library while keeping the pin connections, the scripted equivalent of replacing a part on the page. Combined with the Find commands it allows scripted part-family changes.

parameters.name: libName / pkgName / partName / device
parameters.description: Target library, package, part and device designator.

tools.notes: Record the action once with journaling to confirm the argument order your release emits.

tools.name: PlaceWire
tools.description: Draws a wire segment between two points on the active schematic page, the command the application note uses to illustrate journaling. Chains of segments are placed with successive calls.
tools.notes: Endpoints must land on grid and on pin ends to connect; use the journal of a manual wire to learn the coordinate units of your page.

tools.name: PlaceBus / PlaceBusEntry
tools.description: Draw a bus segment between two points, and place a bus entry at a point (with a flag for its orientation, as journaled). Bus members still need net aliases to connect.

tools.name: PlaceJunction / PlaceNoConnect
tools.description: Place a junction dot at a wire crossing, or a no-connect marker on a pin end, at the given coordinates.

tools.name: PlaceNetAlias
tools.description: Places a net alias label on a wire or bus at a point, naming the net; PlaceNetAliasWithDialog x y opens the Place Net Alias dialog instead. It is the scripted way to name nets in generated schematics.

parameters.name: netAlias
parameters.description: Net name, or bus name with range such as A[0..15].

tools.name: PlacePower / PlaceGround
tools.description: Place a power or ground symbol from a library with a given net name; the symbol name selects the graphic (e.g. VCC_ARROW, GND) and the name sets the global net. The *WithDialog variants open the dialogs; PlaceNetgroupPower/Ground handle NetGroup members.
tools.notes: For PSpice designs the ground net must be named 0 (the '0' symbol from SOURCE.OLB).

tools.name: PlacePort / PlaceOffPage
tools.description: Place a hierarchical port or an off-page connector symbol with a name, connecting nets across hierarchy levels or across pages of a schematic folder. *WithDialog and PlaceNetgroupPort/PlaceNetgroupOffPage variants exist.

tools.name: PlaceBlock
tools.description: Draws a hierarchical block rectangle and binds it to an implementation (schematic view, VHDL, Verilog, PSpice model...), as Place > Hierarchical Block does. PlaceBlockWithDialog opens the dialog after drawing.

parameters.name: viewName
parameters.description: Implementation name, e.g. the child schematic folder.

tools.example: Draw one block by hand with journaling on and replay the echoed PlaceBlock line for each channel of a multi-channel design.

tools.name: PlaceText / PlaceLine / PlaceRectangle / PlaceEllipse / PlaceArc / PlacePolyline / PlacePicture
tools.description: Graphic and annotation placement commands: text in a box, lines, rectangles, ellipses, arcs (four points), polylines and polygons (continued with PlaceNextPolylinePoint / PlaceNextPolygonPoint), Bezier curves and bitmap pictures from a file.
tools.usage:
PlaceText <x1> <y1> <x2> <y2> <commentText>
PlaceLine <x1> <y1> <x2> <y2>
PlaceRectangle <x1> <y1> <x2> <y2>
PlaceArc <x1> <y1> <x2> <y2> <x3> <y3> <x4> <y4>
PlacePolyline <x1> <y1> <x2> <y2>; PlaceNextPolylinePoint <x> <y>
PlacePicture <x> <y> <fileName>
tools.example:
PlaceRectangle 0.50 0.50 4.00 3.00
PlaceText 0.60 0.60 3.90 0.90 {ANALOG FRONT END - DO NOT MOVE}

tools.name: PlaceTitleBlock / PlaceBookMark
tools.description: Place a title block symbol from a library, or a named bookmark that GoToBookMark and Edit > Go To can jump to. Custom page scripts use PlaceTitleBlock to frame pages automatically.

tools.name: PlacePin (Part Editor)
tools.description: Places a pin on the part being edited in the Part Editor with a name and pin type; PlacePinWithDialog opens the Place Pin dialog. It allows scripted symbol generation from pin lists.

parameters.name: pinType
parameters.description: Electrical type as journaled (e.g. Input, Output, Bidirectional, Passive, Power).

tools.example: foreach {n y} {VIN 0.1 GND 0.2 VOUT 0.3} { PlacePin 0.00 $y $n Passive FALSE }
tools.notes: Journal a manual pin placement to see the exact type keywords and flag your release expects.

tools.name: SelectObject / UnSelectObject
tools.description: Select (or deselect) the object at a page coordinate; the boolean argument controls whether the object is added to the existing selection. Selection commands are the prerequisite for Move, Rotate, property and delete commands.

tools.name: SelectBlock / SelectAll / UnSelectAll
tools.description: Area and global selection: SelectBlock selects every object inside a rectangle (note the argument order x1 x2 y1 y2 in the appendix), SelectAll selects everything on the page and UnSelectAll clears the selection.

tools.name: SelectObjectById
tools.description: Selects an object by its database id (dbid) rather than by coordinates, with optional update and probe flags. It bridges database scripts (Dbo* iteration) and GUI commands that act on the selection.

tools.name: GetSelectedObjects
tools.description: Returns a Tcl list of the currently selected database objects, which can then be queried with Dbo* methods (for example DboBaseObject_GetObjectType). It is the standard entry point of context-menu scripts registered with RegisterAction.
tools.notes: In the app-note example, object types 12 and 13 identify placed part instances and hierarchical blocks.

tools.name: FindParts / FindNets / FindPins / FindOffPageConnectors / FindHierarchicalPorts / FindBookMarks / FindDRCMarks / FindText
tools.description: Search commands equivalent to Edit > Find restricted to one object type; matching objects are selected (multiple matches form a selection set). The boolean is the match-case flag, and the value accepts wildcards like the Find toolbar.
tools.usage: FindParts <value> <boolMatchCase>   (same form for FindNets, FindPins, FindOffPageConnectors, FindHierarchicalPorts, FindBookMarks, FindDRCMarks, FindText)
tools.notes: CapFindObjects objType strFindWhat returns results as a Tcl object for scripted processing; capFindSaveInCSV saves the Find window results.

tools.name: Cut / Copy / Paste / Delete / Duplicate
tools.description: Clipboard and edit commands acting on the current selection: Paste and Duplicate take a target location.

tools.name: Move / Drag / Rotate / MirrorHorizontal / MirrorVertical
tools.description: Transform the selection: Move relocates without stretching wires, Drag keeps connections rubber-banded, Rotate turns 90 degrees, and the mirror commands flip horizontally or vertically.
tools.example:
SelectObject 2.00 1.00 FALSE
Drag 2.00 2.00 FALSE
SetOptionBool RotateInstPropInContext ON
Rotate
tools.notes: The app note rotates with RotateInstPropInContext temporarily ON so part properties stay readable after rotation.

tools.name: SetColor / SetLineStyle / SetLineWidth / SetFillStyle / SetHatchStyle / SetFont
tools.description: Change the appearance of selected graphics or text: colour, line style and width, fill and hatch style by numeric id, and font face, height and bold/italic flags.
tools.usage: SetColor <nColorId> | SetLineStyle <id> | SetLineWidth <id> | SetFillStyle <id> | SetHatchStyle <id> | SetFont <Facename> <nHeight> <bool> <bool>
tools.notes: Id values correspond to entries in the Capture colour/style lists; journal a manual change to find the id.

tools.name: ZoomIn / ZoomOut / ZoomArea / ZoomAll / ZoomSelection / ZoomScale
tools.description: View commands for the active page: step zoom in/out, zoom to a rectangle, fit all, zoom to the selection, or set an explicit scale.
tools.usage: ZoomIn | ZoomOut | ZoomArea <x1> <y1> <x2> <y2> | ZoomAll | ZoomSelection | ZoomScale <nscale>

tools.name: GoToAbsolute / GoToRelative / GoToGridReference / GoToBookMark
tools.description: Move the view/pointer to an absolute or relative location, to a grid reference cell, or to a named bookmark, like Edit > Go To.

tools.name: SetProperty / GetProperty / RemoveProperty
tools.description: Set, read or remove an instance property on the selected object(s), the scripted equivalent of editing a cell in the Property Editor for the selection.
tools.notes: Use SetOccProperty/GetOccProperty for occurrence (per-hierarchy-instance) values in occurrence-mode designs.

tools.name: SetOccProperty / GetOccProperty / RemoveOccProperty
tools.description: Occurrence-level versions of the property commands, acting on the property value of the selected object for its current hierarchical occurrence, as used by complex hierarchies where the same block appears several times with different reference designators or values.

tools.name: AddProperty / ModifyProperty / DeleteProperty
tools.description: Path-based property commands that address an object by its hierarchical path instead of by selection, with ModifyProperty taking an occurrence flag. They suit batch edits driven by a list of reference paths.

parameters.name: PathName
parameters.description: Hierarchical path of the object as shown in the Property Editor.

parameters.name: occ
parameters.description: Whether the value is written at occurrence level.

tools.notes: Note the reversed argument order of DeleteProperty (name first). Confirm path syntax by journaling a Property Editor edit.

tools.name: SetDisplayType / RemoveDisplayProperty
tools.description: Control how a property of the selected object is shown on the page (do not display, value only, name and value, name only, both-if-value-exists) or remove its display entirely, like the Display button of the Property Editor.
tools.notes: Journal a manual Display change to get the exact DisplayValue keyword.

tools.name: ShowSpreadsheet / DumpSpreadsheet / SwitchTab
tools.description: Open the Property Editor spreadsheet for the selection, switch its tab (Parts, Schematic Nets, Pins, Title Blocks...) and dump its contents to a file for review or diffing.

tools.name: Open / CloseProject / Exit
tools.description: Open a project, design or library file by path, close the active project, or exit Capture. Together with TclScript they let a batch job open a design, run edits and quit.
tools.notes: IsDocModified returns non-zero when the active document has unsaved changes, so a batch loop can decide whether to save before CloseProject.

tools.name: NDesign / NSchematic / NPage / OPage
tools.description: Project Manager commands to create a new design, a new schematic folder or a new page in a folder, and to open an existing page (optionally a specific occurrence). Scripts use them to build multi-page designs automatically.
tools.example:
NPage SCHEMATIC1 POWER
OPage SCHEMATIC1 POWER
PlaceWire 1 1 3 1

tools.name: GetActivePage / GetActivePMDesign / GetActiveOpjName / GetActiveView
tools.description: Return the active schematic page (DboPage), the design open in the active Project Manager (DboDesign), the active .opj name and the active view, linking GUI context to the Dbo database API.
tools.usage: set p [GetActivePage] | set d [GetActivePMDesign] | GetActiveOpjName | GetActiveView
tools.example:
set lPage [GetActivePage]
set lStatus [DboState]
set it [$lPage NewPartInstsIter $lStatus]

tools.name: SelectPMItem / GetSelectedPMItems / GetPMItemName / GetPMItemType
tools.description: Select an item in the Project Manager tree by name and query the selected items, their names and types, which is how scripts target a particular folder, page or library before running a Tools command.

tools.name: GetProductVersion / GetToolName / GetLicenseString
tools.description: Return the Capture version, the tool/product name and the license string in use, so scripts can branch on release or license tier (for example CIS-only features).

tools.name: GetOptionBool / GetOptionString / SetOptionString / GetOptionUInt / SetOptionUInt
tools.description: Read and write Capture options (the settings persisted in Capture.ini) by name, complementing SetOptionBool. Used to toggle behaviours such as journaling or in-context property rotation around a script.
tools.example:
set old [GetOptionBool Journaling]
SetOptionBool Journaling TRUE

tools.name: GetEnv / SetEnv / GetIniPath
tools.description: Read or set environment variables inside the Capture process and return the path of the Capture.ini in use (by default %HOME%/cdssetup/OrCAD_Capture/<release>).

tools.name: AskUserInput / capDisplayMessageBox
tools.description: Minimal user interaction from scripts: AskUserInput shows a prompt with a default value and returns the text entered; capDisplayMessageBox shows a Windows message box with a caption and optional button type (default MB_OK) and returns the choice.
tools.example:
set pfx [AskUserInput {Reference prefix} U]
capDisplayMessageBox "Renamed parts with $pfx" {Script done}

tools.name: ClearSessionLog / DumpSessionLog
tools.description: Clear the Session Log window, or write its contents to a file, typically around a netlist, DRC or annotation run so a script can parse the messages.

tools.name: RegisterAction
tools.description: Adds a custom item to Capture's right-mouse-button pop-up menu: a label, an enabler procedure returning 1 or 0, an accelerator (currently unused), the callback procedure, and the view type (Schematic, PM, or empty). Special labels such as _cdnCapTclAddPageCustomMenu hook scripts that add Accessories menus.

parameters.name: Enabler
parameters.description: Tcl proc; return 1 to enable the item for the current selection.

tools.notes: Introduced in Capture 16.3. Put the registration in a capAutoLoad script so it is available in every session.

tools.name: AddAccessoryMenu
tools.description: Adds a vendor/user submenu and command under Capture's Accessories menu, bound to a Tcl callback. Page-level callbacks receive the page and occurrence, design-level callbacks receive the library/design object.
tools.example:
proc ::my::openNotepad {pLib} { exec notepad.exe }
AddAccessoryMenu "Text Editors" "Design in Notepad" "::my::openNotepad"
tools.notes: In the app note it is called from procedures registered with RegisterAction "_cdnCapTclAddDesignCustomMenu" or "_cdnCapTclAddPageCustomMenu".

tools.name: TclScript / Shell
tools.description: TclScript runs a Tcl script file through Capture's command machinery; Shell launches an external application with optional arguments and returns its result, for example to open a report in an editor or call a converter.
tools.notes: Standard Tcl 'source' and 'exec' also work; brace-quote Windows paths.

tools.name: capSaveCompleteProject
tools.description: Saves a complete copy of the active project to a destination directory, optionally under a new project name and including library files, output files, referenced projects and test benches: a scripted archive or 'save project as'.

tools.name: capBatchAnnotate
tools.description: Runs Annotate from a script, either with the current dialog settings (no arguments) or with explicit scope, update type (incremental, unconditional, reset...), combined property strings and the option flags of the Annotate dialog.

parameters.name: cstrCombinedProperty
parameters.description: Combined property string used to group parts into packages, e.g. {Value}{Source Package}{POWER_GROUP}.

tools.notes: Numeric codes for scope and update type follow the order of the Annotate dialog options; verify on a copy of the design.

tools.name: svsDiffDesigns
tools.description: Compares two designs and reports differences, the engine behind the Design Difference Viewer, with options for occurrence mode and ECO mode. Useful in scripted release checks between revisions.

tools.name: CreateTestBench
tools.description: Creates a test bench for partial design simulation (the scripted form of Tools > Test Bench > Create Test Bench), optionally with a given name; the test bench appears under TestBenches in the Project Manager.
tools.notes: A default name can be set in Capture.ini: [TEST BENCH] Default Test Bench Name=<name>.

tools.name: CapPdfPrint / CapPdfSetOption / CapPdfGetOption
tools.description: Script interface of Capture's PDF export: set or read PDF export options, then write the PDF to an output directory and file name. CapPdfAddMarkStart/Data/End add custom bookmarks or annotations to regions.
tools.notes: Option names match the File > Export > PDF dialog settings of your release; read them back with CapPdfGetOption.

tools.name: CapCustomDRCElectricalAddItem / CapCustomDRCPhysicalAddItem
tools.description: Register custom Design Rules Check items implemented in Tcl, under the Electrical or Physical rules of the DRC dialog, with an execute flag and an OK callback. capGetDRCList returns the registered checks.
tools.notes: Listed in the Capture command list of the Tcl application note; which releases expose custom DRC items in the DRC dialog varies, so check that the registered item appears after sourcing the script.
